title: PostgreSQL connection pooling with PgBouncer
text: PgBouncer sits between the application and Postgres and multiplexes many client connections onto a small number of server connections. Transaction pooling mode gives the highest reuse but breaks session-level features such as prepared statements and advisory locks. Size default_pool_size from the CPU cores of the database host, not from the number of application pods.

title: Fixing 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already'
text: This PostgreSQL error means max_connections has been reached. Raising max_connections is rarely the right fix because each backend process consumes memory; put a connection pooler in front of the database instead and audit application code for leaked connections that are never returned.

title: PostgreSQL VACUUM and table bloat
text: Postgres uses MVCC, so updated and deleted rows leave dead tuples behind. Autovacuum reclaims them; if it falls behind, tables bloat and queries slow down. Lower autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor for large, frequently updated tables.

title: Choosing PostgreSQL index types
text: B-tree indexes handle equality and range queries and are the default. GIN indexes suit jsonb containment and full-text search, BRIN indexes are tiny and work well for naturally ordered data such as append-only timestamps, and HNSW indexes from pgvector support approximate nearest-neighbour search over embeddings.

title: Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff
text: CrashLoopBackOff means a container starts, exits, and is restarted by the kubelet with an exponentially increasing delay. Check kubectl logs --previous for the output of the last crash and kubectl describe pod for the exit code; exit code 137 indicates the container was killed, often by the OOM killer.

title: Kubernetes OOMKilled and memory limits
text: When a container exceeds its memory limit the kernel OOM killer terminates it and the pod status shows OOMKilled with exit code 137. Set requests to typical usage and limits with headroom for peaks; for JVM workloads, size the heap below the container limit with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage.

title: Kubernetes liveness vs readiness probes
text: A readiness probe decides whether a pod receives traffic from a Service; a failing readiness probe removes the pod from the endpoints without restarting it. A liveness probe restarts the container when it fails. Never point a liveness probe at a dependency such as the database, or a database outage will restart every pod in the fleet.

title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
text: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales the number of replicas based on observed metrics such as CPU utilisation or custom metrics from Prometheus. It requires resource requests to be set, because utilisation is computed as a percentage of the request.

title: Redis eviction policies
text: When Redis reaches maxmemory it applies the configured maxmemory-policy. allkeys-lru evicts the least recently used keys across the whole keyspace and suits caches; volatile-lru only evicts keys that have a TTL; noeviction returns errors on writes, which is the right choice when Redis is used as a primary data store.

title: Cache stampede protection
text: When a popular cache entry expires, many requests can miss at the same moment and overload the database: a cache stampede, also called a thundering herd. Mitigations include request coalescing with a single flight per key, probabilistic early expiration, and serving the stale value while one worker refreshes the entry.

title: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
text: A 429 status code means the client exceeded a rate limit. Well-behaved clients read the Retry-After header and back off; combine exponential backoff with random jitter so that retries from many clients do not synchronise into waves.

title: Idempotency keys for safe retries
text: Retrying a POST request can create duplicate side effects such as double charges. The client sends a unique Idempotency-Key header; the server stores the result for that key and returns the same response for repeated requests instead of executing the operation twice.

title: Token bucket rate limiting
text: The token bucket algorithm refills tokens at a fixed rate up to a burst capacity; each request consumes a token and is rejected when the bucket is empty. It tolerates short bursts while enforcing an average rate, unlike a fixed window counter, which can admit double the limit around window boundaries.

title: JWT validation checklist
text: Always verify the signature with the expected algorithm, never accept alg=none, and validate the exp, nbf, iss and aud claims. Keep access tokens short-lived and fetch signing keys from the issuer's JWKS endpoint, caching them while respecting key rotation.

title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE
text: Public clients such as single-page and mobile apps cannot keep a client secret. PKCE binds the authorization code to a code_verifier generated by the client, so an intercepted code cannot be exchanged for tokens by an attacker.

title: Storing passwords
text: Hash passwords with a slow, memory-hard function such as Argon2id, or bcrypt, with a unique salt per user. Never use fast hashes like SHA-256 for passwords, and never store them with reversible encryption.

title: Python GIL and concurrency
text: The global interpreter lock lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time, so threads do not speed up CPU-bound pure-Python code. Use multiprocessing or native extensions for CPU-bound work; threads and asyncio remain effective for I/O-bound workloads because the GIL is released while waiting on I/O.

title: asyncio: avoiding blocking calls
text: Calling a blocking function such as time.sleep or a synchronous HTTP client inside a coroutine freezes the entire event loop. Use await asyncio.sleep, async libraries, or move the blocking work to a thread with asyncio.to_thread.

title: Python memory leak debugging
text: Use tracemalloc to take snapshots of allocations and compare them over time to find the lines whose memory keeps growing. Common culprits are unbounded caches, global lists that accumulate items, and reference cycles that hold large objects.

title: ModuleNotFoundError in virtual environments
text: ModuleNotFoundError usually means the interpreter running the code is not the one the package was installed into. Run python -m pip --version to see which environment pip targets, and invoke tools as python -m pytest so they use the active interpreter.

title: Prometheus histogram vs summary
text: Histograms record observations into configurable buckets and can be aggregated across instances, so service-wide percentiles can be computed with histogram_quantile. Summaries compute quantiles inside each client and cannot be meaningfully aggregated.

title: Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry
text: OpenTelemetry propagates trace context, the W3C traceparent header, across service calls so spans from many services join into a single trace. Sample at the head for cost control, or use tail-based sampling in the collector to keep slow and failed traces.

title: Alerting on SLOs with burn rates
text: Instead of alerting on raw error-rate thresholds, alert on how fast the error budget is being spent. A multi-window burn-rate alert, for example 14.4x over both 1 hour and 5 minutes, pages quickly for severe incidents while ignoring short blips.

title: Blue-green vs canary deployments
text: Blue-green deployment keeps two full environments and switches traffic all at once, which makes rollback instant. Canary releases shift a small percentage of traffic to the new version and increase it gradually while watching error rates and latency.

title: Git: recovering a deleted branch
text: Commits from a deleted branch remain reachable through the reflog for a while. Run git reflog to find the commit hash at the tip of the branch, then git branch <name> <hash> to restore it.

title: Docker image size reduction
text: Use multi-stage builds so compilers and build dependencies stay out of the final image, start from slim or distroless base images, and combine package installation and cleanup in a single layer. A .dockerignore file keeps the build context small.

title: BM25 ranking function
text: BM25 scores a document by summing, over the query terms, the inverse document frequency times a saturated term frequency. The k1 parameter controls how quickly term frequency saturates and b controls document length normalisation; typical values are k1 between 1.2 and 2.0 and b = 0.75.

title: Dense retrieval with bi-encoders
text: A bi-encoder embeds queries and documents independently into vectors, so document embeddings can be precomputed and searched with approximate nearest-neighbour indexes. Dense retrieval matches paraphrases and synonyms that lexical search misses, but it can fail on rare identifiers, product codes and exact phrases.

title: Hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion
text: Hybrid search runs lexical and dense retrieval in parallel and merges their results. Reciprocal rank fusion scores each document by summing 1/(k + rank) over the result lists, which avoids having to calibrate BM25 scores against cosine similarities.

title: Cross-encoder rerankers
text: A cross-encoder feeds the query and a candidate passage through a transformer together and outputs a relevance score. Because every query token attends to every passage token it is far more accurate than a bi-encoder, but it must run once per candidate, so it is applied only to the top few dozen results of a first-stage retriever.

title: ColBERT late interaction
text: ColBERT stores one embedding per token for every passage and scores relevance with MaxSim: each query token is matched to its most similar passage token and the maxima are summed. It keeps much of a cross-encoder's accuracy while allowing passage representations to be precomputed.

title: Chunking documents for RAG
text: Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding and waste the context window; chunks that are too small lose the surrounding context needed to answer. Split on natural boundaries such as headings and paragraphs, add a small overlap, and keep a pointer from each chunk to its parent document.

title: Evaluating retrieval quality
text: Measure retrieval separately from generation. Recall@k tells you whether the right passage reached the candidate set at all; nDCG@10 and MRR measure whether it is ranked near the top. Build a labelled set of real user queries before tuning anything.

title: Lost in the middle
text: Language models use information at the beginning and end of a long context more reliably than information in the middle. Reranking and passing fewer, more relevant passages often improves answer quality more than adding more context.

title: Kafka consumer lag
text: Consumer lag is the difference between the latest offset in a partition and the offset the consumer group has committed. Growing lag means consumers cannot keep up; add consumers up to the number of partitions, since each partition is consumed by at most one member of a group.

title: Exactly-once semantics in Kafka
text: Kafka's idempotent producer prevents duplicates caused by retries within a partition, and transactions let a consume-transform-produce pipeline commit output messages and consumer offsets atomically. End-to-end exactly-once still requires idempotent writes in external sinks.

title: TLS certificate expired errors
text: Errors such as x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid mean the presented certificate is outside its validity window, or the client clock is wrong. Automate renewal with an ACME client such as cert-manager and alert well before expiry.

title: DNS TTL and failover
text: Clients and resolvers cache DNS answers for the record's TTL, so DNS-based failover cannot take effect faster than the TTL allows. Lower TTLs ahead of planned migrations, and note that some clients ignore TTLs and cache for longer.

title: Feature flags
text: Feature flags decouple deploying code from releasing features, enabling gradual rollouts, kill switches and A/B tests. Remove stale flags promptly, because accumulated flags create combinatorial complexity and dead code.

title: Database migrations without downtime
text: Use the expand-and-contract pattern: add new columns or tables first, deploy code that writes to both the old and new schema, backfill, switch reads, then remove the old schema in a later release. Avoid long-running locks on large tables during the migration.

title: PostgreSQL max_connections setting overview
text: The max_connections parameter sets the maximum number of concurrent connections to the database server and can only be changed with a server restart. Its default value is typically 100 connections.

title: Kubernetes probe configuration fields
text: Probes support initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, successThreshold and failureThreshold. A probe handler can be an HTTP GET, a TCP socket check, a gRPC health check, or an exec command run inside the container.

title: Redis persistence: RDB and AOF
text: RDB snapshots write the dataset to disk at intervals, while AOF logs every write operation so it can be replayed on restart. Many deployments enable both to balance durability against fast restarts.

title: Python threading module basics
text: threading.Thread runs a callable in a new thread; call join() to wait for it and use a Lock to protect shared state. The concurrent.futures ThreadPoolExecutor offers a higher-level interface for running many tasks on threads.
